title: Production agents need measured behaviour, not carefully worded prompts alone
friendlyTitle: Test what an AI agent does instead of trusting its prompt
summary: A production-agent engineering talk argues that prompts are unstable components whose effects change with surrounding instructions, models and product revisions. It recommends repeated pass-to-the-k testing, adversarial scenarios, usage monitoring and optimisation against explicit measures rather than treating a prompt as a durable policy.
friendlySummary: A prompt that works today may fail after other instructions or the model change. The author recommends running many tests and measuring the behaviour people actually need.
whyItMatters: Teams can spend weeks polishing instructions while missing rare failures that appear only at scale. Converting desired behaviour into repeatable tests makes agent changes reviewable and helps distinguish a real improvement from a prompt that merely worked once.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Good wording is not a safety system. Repeated tests show whether an agent remains useful and reliable across many real situations.
